- Allergy: usually hives, sneezing, watery eyes. Reference [15] mentions runny nose, sneeze, sore/watery eyes, hoarse voice, headache.
- Drug reaction: rashes, flake off, prone to infection, fingers twitch, shake. Ref [3]. Or tremors, muscle twitching, fatigue, rapid heartbeat. Ref [11].

Chicken pox fits best. The symptoms "red spots all over my body", "itchy", "fever", "headache", "exhausted" align with chicken pox. Reference [1] is extremely similar: "little red spots all over my body... exhausted and have a severe headache." -> chicken pox.

Reference [1] explicitly links "red spots all over my body", "exhausted", "severe headache" to chicken pox.
Reference [12] links "red spots all over my body", "very itchy", "extreme body pain, headache and vomiting" to dengue.
Our prompt lacks "extreme body pain" and "vomiting", but has "fever, headache, and feel exhausted". So chicken pox is more appropriate.

- fungal infection: lacks flaking, different colored patches.
- drug reaction: lacks history of medication, twitching/shaking.
- allergy: lacks respiratory symptoms (sneezing, runny nose), though can cause itchy spots, chicken pox is a better fit for fever + exhaustion + red spots.

Therefore, chicken pox is the most accurate diagnosis.
